# MiddleLeap

> MiddleLeap is an independent advisory firm based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It helps banks, fintechs, financial infrastructure providers, telecommunications companies and other regulated platform businesses move from strategic mandate to market execution.

Canonical website: https://www.middleleap.com/
Contact: contact@middleleap.com
Founded: 2021
Founder: Michael Ryberg Hartmann
Primary market: Middle East and North Africa

## Positioning

MiddleLeap helps leaders turn regulatory, commercial and technology shifts into platform advantage. Its work connects market position, platform economics, ecosystem design and AI-native operating models. Open Finance is a significant area of experience, but it is one part of the broader regulated platform transformation practice.

## Core capabilities

- Regulatory and market transformation: Open Finance strategy, regulatory readiness, LFI and TPP operating models, market entry and ecosystem participation.
- Platform and ecosystem strategy: platform propositions, API strategy, embedded finance, partnerships, commercial models and monetisation.
- AI-native operating models: value-stream redesign, agentic workflows, product and engineering models, governance and control.
- Transformation and execution: executive mobilisation, programme leadership, platform delivery, organization design and delivery modernisation.

### Open Finance advisory

MiddleLeap helps banks, fintechs, TPPs and financial infrastructure providers connect Open Finance obligations with market position, propositions, ecosystem economics, platform capabilities and accountable execution.

- Market position: decide where the institution will lead, participate or partner as regulation changes the value chain.
- Proposition: translate permitted data and payment capabilities into customer, partner and embedded-finance propositions.
- Platform: shape the consent, data, API, partner and control capabilities required to operate at ecosystem scale.
- Operating model: align product, technology, risk, compliance, operations and partner management around accountable execution.
- Engagement models include executive advisory, focused strategy sprints and transformation mobilisation.

## How MiddleLeap works

MiddleLeap works from mandate to working capability through five stages:

1. Frame the regulatory, commercial or operating mandate.
2. Design the proposition, ecosystem, platform and operating model.
3. Mobilise leaders, partners, product teams and governance stakeholders.
4. Deliver working products and capabilities.
5. Codify reusable knowledge, controls and agent workflows.

One practice runs three connected systems. Advisory frames the strategic, regulatory and commercial mandate. Execution turns it into working capability through The Loom and The Loom Toolkit. Ventures test propositions in operating reality, and the learning returns to Advisory to sharpen the next mandate.

The Loom is MiddleLeap's governed route from an ambiguous mandate to accountable software. Discovery and Delivery are its two harnesses. A third arc, Run and Operations, returns incidents, drift, regulatory change and customer signals to Discovery as evidence, so the institution learns from what the software actually does.

The Loom is the governed delivery method. The Loom Toolkit is the installable product that carries the method, controls and adoption machinery into a repository. AI-DLC is the technical distribution mechanism for the Toolkit rather than a separate consulting proposition. The Institutional BrainKit is the institution-owned context component, and domain packs are optional specialist intelligence.

### The Loom

- Two harnesses form a double diamond. Discovery diverges around evidence and converges on one problem through gates D1-D9; Delivery diverges across solutions and converges under control through quality gates Q1-Q5. They meet at one enforced waist gate: a gate-green hand-off. Discovery may stop a weak problem early, and delivery evidence may legitimately send the work back.
- Discovery gates D1-D9 cover framing, evidence, scope, the no-solutioning boundary, synthesis, data governance, brand conformance, tangibility and stakeholder validation. Prototypes are brand-real and behaviour-hollow: they test the framing without binding the production solution.
- Delivery is spec-first and agent-enabled. Contract, generated types and acceptance tests precede implementation; bounded reviewers judge hard stops and contract conformance; PII, spec and test-integrity tripwires apply at the moment of edit; and a protected control plane keeps merge approval accountable, per change by default or through a narrowly governed routine-change envelope in which approval is relocated, never removed.
- A third arc, Run and Operations, deploys, observes and triages. Most signals become a delivery fix or a risk-register update; only evidence that challenges the original framing reopens Discovery.
- The control chain runs mandate, problem, solution, release, outcome and signal. The success measures that justify the problem become the evaluation targets for the released product, and every step leaves an owned artifact.
- The context brain is the pattern the harness weaves to. It has three dimensions: mandate context, solution-domain knowledge and institutional DNA.
- Continuous assurance re-runs on changes, schedules and regulatory events through watch, assess, check, test, evidence and confirm, closing with agent-prepared reporting plus human four-eyes.
- Harness governance is a stated catalogue of thirteen decisions, including no self-merge, immutable controls, sealed evidence, least privilege, governed promotion, model-risk governance of the harness itself, a discovery-first entry condition, residency control and a mandatory kill switch with a named accountable officer.
- Control maturity is graded honestly: absent, defined, mechanically validated, platform enforced and organisationally enforced. Documentation alone is not treated as enforcement.
- The first evidenced implementation was the Open Finance Backoffice, where 134 of approximately 139 stories reached done under quality gates, synthetic-data constraints and human four-eyes merge.
- The stated limits are plain. The proof is demo-proven, not production-proven, and has not cleared live production scale or a regulator examination. One domain is early evidence. Delivery spend is measured while value remains unproven. Comprehension debt remains. The context brain must be curated. AI model risk requires validation, monitoring and independent challenge.

### The Loom Toolkit

- Core bundle: the discovery and delivery harnesses, the Institutional BrainKit, compiled control plans, continuous assurance, governance and evidence controls, and safe, merge-aware adoption from one copy manifest.
- Institutional BrainKit: a private, human-approved package of institutional terminology, architecture, technology policy, design standards and decision rights. It is drafted from approved sources only with unknowns left visible as gaps, approved by accountable owners, digest-pinned per repository and validated in CI.
- Open Finance Intelligence domain pack: CBUAE and AlTareq knowledge, Islamic-banking context, UAE bank risk review and value-proposition prototyping, attached only when a mandate requires it.
- AI-DLC: the repository and plugin mechanism used to distribute, version and adopt the public Toolkit.
- Operating boundary: the Toolkit is a build-time control frame. It validates repository-level gates, evidence and readiness records; live IAM, platform enforcement, production monitoring, incident detection, resilience exercises and independent control functions remain the adopting institution's responsibility.

## Ventures, portfolio and studio

MiddleLeap builds and contributes to working platforms so its advisory work is grounded in operating evidence. The primary portfolio is one flagship regulated proof, two venture experiments and one compounding body of evidence:

- Open Finance Backoffice — flagship regulated proof, regulated delivery profile, demo-complete. A bank-neutral, synthetic-only operating platform that turns Open Finance obligations into governed workflows for people and agents, and the first formal proof of the harness.
- Parqo — venture experiment, venture delivery profile, acquisition wedge live. A UAE parking marketplace beginning with a live demand-and-supply acquisition wedge in dense business districts. It is not yet an operating marketplace; commercial investment is gated by district-level demand and supply evidence.
- HiveMind / Hive Coach — venture experiment, venture delivery profile, initial product live. A human-led coaching product that turns track evidence into grounded, coach-owned advice, testing how AI can extend an expert service without taking authority from the expert.

Parqo and HiveMind apply The Loom's evidence, specification and human-authority principles to venture building. Neither is a claim of full regulated-harness adoption.

OpenFinance-OS, the Data Sandbox and Ecosystem Watcher are presented separately as independent ecosystem contributions. MiddleLeap's role is contribution and stewardship, not institutional ownership.

The MiddleLeap Venture Studio invites operators, domain experts and potential partners to propose non-confidential, evidenced problems in regulated markets, platform businesses and financial infrastructure. Dubai is the base and MENA the primary market; this is for evidenced problems, not funding-only pitch submissions. Submissions are screened before any evidence sprint, venture thesis or bounded pilot, and the outcome may be a venture, a partnership, shared infrastructure, an advisory mandate or an explicit decision not to proceed.

The portfolio operates as a build, learn and apply loop: build working assets, capture market and execution intelligence, and apply the learning to client mandates.

## Engagement models

- Executive advisory for regulatory, platform and transformation mandates.
- Platform strategy sprints covering proposition, ecosystem, commercial model and execution roadmap.
- AI-native delivery pilots that adopt The Loom around one bounded outcome and leave a governed repository capability behind.

## Experience and delivery model

- MiddleLeap is a founder-led, networked advisory practice rather than a fixed consulting bench.
- Each mandate has senior accountability, specialists assembled around the problem and active client leadership so institutional context and delivery capability remain with the client.
- Experience carried into the practice includes building and expanding an Open Banking platform across MENA, followed by leadership of a dual LFI/TPP programme that helped a leading UAE bank achieve first-bank certification under the UAE Open Finance framework and deliver the country's first live transactions with a licensed TPP.
- Business-banking ecosystem experience includes the build-out of Danske Bank's District platform and marketplace across the Nordics and UK, the migration of 250,000 SMEs, corporates and institutions, and the development of API-based partner channels.
- Enterprise transformation experience includes leadership of a 70+ person digital delivery organization through an API-first Telco-as-a-Service shift within a 140-year-old company.
- MiddleLeap was founded by Michael Ryberg Hartmann, a product and technology executive with more than 20 years across banking, fintech, telecommunications and SaaS. He leads selected mandates and assembles the senior specialists required around each client and problem.
- Professional profile: https://www.linkedin.com/in/michael-ryberg-hartmann
